title: Telecom Indicators and annual subscriber statistics
research_use: Mobile broadband, cellular coverage, subscriber growth, and infrastructure context.
claim_supported: Digital distribution became materially more feasible as mobile broadband expanded.
limitation: Historical tables need to be downloaded and standardized to a consistent month or fiscal-year endpoint; the live website can render values dynamically.

title: $1.1 billion raised from 3G, 4G auction
source_type: Contemporaneous journalism based on PTA results
research_use: Anchor event for the mobile broadband transition.
claim_supported: Pakistan concluded its first major 3G and 4G spectrum auction on 23 April 2014.
limitation: Use PTA licensing records for legal and technical detail; the article is an event report rather than a longitudinal dataset.

title: PTA Annual Report: Telecom revenues reach record Rs 955 billion in FY 2023-24
source_type: Government news summary of official annual report
research_use: Recent broadband, mobile, coverage, and infrastructure benchmarks.
claim_supported: By 2024 Pakistan had a very large mobile broadband base and extensive 3G/4G coverage.
limitation: Extract exact values from the underlying PTA annual report before statistical use.

title: YouTube to be unblocked within 48 hours: PTA
source_type: Contemporaneous journalism citing government and regulator
research_use: Anchor event for restoration of the country’s largest music-video distribution channel.
claim_supported: The government directed restoration of YouTube access in January 2016 after a multi-year ban.
limitation: The localized service remained subject to content restriction; platform availability should not be coded as unrestricted access.

title: Spotify Expands International Footprint, Bringing Audio to 80+ New Markets
research_use: Date and terms of Spotify’s market entry.
claim_supported: Spotify included Pakistan in its 2021 expansion.
limitation: A launch announcement proves availability, not audience size, artist income, or editorial equality.

title: Pakistani Artist Shae Gill Breaks Streaming Records With Viral Hit “Pasoori”
research_use: Platform-recognized global breakthrough case and domestic Wrapped ranking.
claim_supported: “Pasoori” was the most-streamed Pakistani song on Spotify in 2022 and circulated globally.
limitation: The platform provides selected success metrics rather than complete denominators, payout data, or country-level stream shares.

title: Spotify ICON Pakistan
source_type: First-party platform analytics and campaign announcement
research_use: Legacy-catalog revival, audience age composition, and transnational listening examples.
claim_supported: Older Pakistani catalogues can acquire renewed platform attention among younger listeners.
limitation: Figures are campaign-selected and cannot be generalized to the national catalogue without raw platform data.

title: Spotify Pakistan Celebrates Its First Album Launch With Talal Qureshi’s TURBO
research_use: Case of platform promotional support beyond passive hosting.
claim_supported: Spotify provided selected Pakistani artists with international promotional placements.
limitation: A promotional case does not reveal selection criteria, opportunity distribution, or commercial return.

title: Warner Music Partners With Leading Pakistani Music Company Giraffe
research_use: Foreign-label entry, A&R infrastructure, and Coke Studio partnership.
claim_supported: Warner Music formed a partnership with Giraffe and linked it to Coke Studio Season 15.
limitation: Commercial terms, rights splits, artist remuneration, and contract duration are not public.

title: Announcing Coke Studio Season 15
research_use: Programme scale, official cultural-export framing, languages, production, and distribution claims.
claim_supported: Coke Studio functions as a large branded cultural platform with substantial international digital circulation.
limitation: Audience numbers are self-reported aggregate promotional figures; verify against channel-level data and avoid treating them as industry revenue.

title: How Arooj Aftab Made History at the 2022 GRAMMYs
research_use: International recognition and diaspora pathway case.
claim_supported: Arooj Aftab won Best Global Music Performance for “Mohabbat” in 2022.
limitation: An award is symbolic recognition, not evidence of domestic employment growth or industry-wide earnings.

title: The Copyright Ordinance, 1962, as amended in 2000
time_scope: Current legal framework subject to subsequent law and case interpretation
research_use: Definitions of musical works, records, ownership, assignment, public performance, broadcast, and related rights.
claim_supported: Pakistan has a formal copyright framework that covers musical works and sound recordings.
limitation: Legal existence does not establish effective enforcement, collective management, bargaining power, or payment practice.

title: Pakistan’s first music policy prepared to resolve piracy and copyright issues
research_use: Policy agenda, stated rights categories, piracy, preservation, and regional music.
claim_supported: The government prepared a national music-policy draft addressing rights and piracy.
limitation: The source records policy intent, not implementation, budget, enforcement, or outcomes.

title: Cabinet approves draft National Music Policy
research_use: Policy process and approval milestone.
claim_supported: The federal cabinet approved a draft national music policy in August 2023.
limitation: Locate the final gazetted text, implementing rules, responsible agencies, and budget before coding policy implementation.
access_status: Public; final policy text still to locate

title: Patari opens for public
research_use: Local streaming launch, intended revenue sharing, catalogue, and app strategy.
claim_supported: Patari and Taazi emerged as local legal-music distribution experiments in 2015.
limitation: Founders’ plans are not equivalent to realized business performance.

title: Patari makes good on royalties promise
research_use: Early local-streaming royalty-payment evidence.
claim_supported: Patari announced a first-quarter royalty pool allocated by plays.
limitation: The article does not provide audited accounts, per-stream rates, rights splits, or recipient distribution.

title: Patari in hot water over non-payment issues
research_use: Cash-flow, brand dependence, subscription difficulty, and artist-payment disputes.
claim_supported: Local streaming faced monetization and payment-friction problems despite audience growth.
limitation: Disputed claims require interviews, contracts, and accounts; named and anonymous testimony should be triangulated.

title: The minds and machines behind Pakistan’s music industry
research_use: Studios, labels, producers, streaming services, copyright history, and industrial structure.
claim_supported: Pakistan’s music economy was institutionally fragmented and dependent on a small set of intermediaries.
limitation: The article is a rich historical snapshot but must be updated through interviews and records for 2017-2026.

title: The rap star of Karachi: “My veil cannot take away the talent I have”
research_use: Gender, family regulation, class, regional identity, mobile production, Patari, and Coke Studio pathway.
claim_supported: Digital entry and branded exposure can coexist with severe gendered and material constraints.
limitation: A single profile cannot represent all women, Baloch artists, or Lyari; use it as a case, not a population estimate.

title: Composing an Oppositional Discourse in Coke Studio Pakistan
author_or_org: Ryan A. D’Souza, Communication, Culture and Critique
research_use: Gender, mystical Islam, nation image, and oppositional cultural discourse.
claim_supported: Coke Studio can be analyzed as a representation system, not merely as a catalogue of songs.
limitation: The article emphasizes discourse and representation rather than revenue, contracts, or labour outcomes.
access_status: Abstract public; full text may require access

title: Outsourcing the nation? Musical collaboration, nation building and neo-liberal logics in Coke Studio Pakistan
research_use: Corporate patronage, nation branding, network representation, and exclusions.
claim_supported: Corporate sponsorship can perform cultural-institution functions while privileging particular artists and representations.
limitation: Its coding and conclusions should be replicated or extended for Seasons 14-15 and the broader industry.

title: YouTube Coke Studio Pakistan: Negotiating Identity, Blurring Boundaries
author_or_org: Munira Cheema, Online Media and Society
time_scope: Selected Coke Studio video and comments
research_use: Cultural citizenship and audience interaction.
claim_supported: YouTube comments can be treated as a platformed public, with careful sampling and ethics.
limitation: Single-video or convenience samples do not represent national audiences; journal standing and methods should be appraised.

title: Popular music as desecuritising discourse: a YouTube analysis of Coke Studio across South Asia
research_use: Cross-border discourse, YouTube Data API design, sentiment and qualitative comment analysis.
claim_supported: Coke Studio audience spaces can contain substantial expressions of cross-border affinity.
limitation: Keyword and sentiment methods are sensitive to multilingual nuance, platform selection, deleted comments, and fandom bias.

title: Music and Transculturalism: Analyzing the Role of Coke Studio Music in Pakistan
author_or_org: Sobia Abid, Muhammad Zahid Bilal, and Aleena Begum
research_use: Audience perceptions of transcultural fusion.
claim_supported: Audience research can test how branded fusion music is interpreted by young listeners.
limitation: Student samples and cross-sectional surveys cannot represent the entire population or establish long-run change.

title: The platformization of cultural production: Theorizing the contingent cultural commodity
author_or_org: David B. Nieborg and Thomas Poell
research_use: Core platformization framework for production, distribution, data feedback, and dependence.
claim_supported: Platform power changes cultural goods, intermediaries, and the conditions of production.
limitation: The original cases are not Pakistani music; the framework must be adapted rather than copied mechanically.

title: Playing to the Crowd: Musicians, Audiences, and the Intimate Work of Connection
research_use: Relational labour, fan connection, self-promotion, and blurred work boundaries.
claim_supported: Direct audience access creates new unpaid or underpaid relationship work for musicians.
limitation: Platform affordances and labour conditions differ by country, gender, class, and infrastructure.

title: The Cultural Industries, Fourth Edition
research_use: Industry structure, risk, ownership, creative autonomy, intermediaries, and inequality.
claim_supported: An industry must be analyzed through institutions and power, not visibility alone.
limitation: Country-specific institutional detail must come from Pakistani evidence.

title: Creative Labour: Media Work in Three Cultural Industries
research_use: Autonomy, self-exploitation, insecurity, emotional labour, and quality of work.
claim_supported: Creative satisfaction and labour precarity can coexist and must be measured separately.
limitation: Interview constructs need contextual translation for Pakistani family, gender, and informal-economy conditions.

title: Why Music Matters
research_use: Social value, commonality, inequality, national identity, and musical flourishing.
claim_supported: Music’s cultural value should be analyzed alongside, not reduced to, market value.
limitation: Normative cultural value is not directly measurable by streams or awards.

title: Nothing personal: algorithmic individuation on music streaming platforms
research_use: Personalization, datafication, and algorithmic audience construction.
claim_supported: Platform discovery is shaped by data and recommender systems rather than neutral public choice.
limitation: Platform algorithms are opaque and change over time; inference requires careful qualification.

title: Locating Power in Platformization: Music Streaming Playlists and Curatorial Power
research_use: Playlist curation, market coordination, and platform power.
claim_supported: Playlist visibility is an institutional outcome, not merely a reflection of listener demand.
limitation: Editorial access and playlist practice in Pakistan require direct platform and artist interviews.

title: Music Platforms and the Optimization of Culture
research_use: How creators and labels adapt sound, release schedules, and metadata to platform incentives.
claim_supported: Platform pressures can reshape music production and release strategy.
limitation: Do not infer optimization in Pakistan from song form alone; ask creators and compare production histories.

title: Global Music Report 2025: recorded music revenues grew in 2024
research_use: Global and Asian streaming context and standardized industry definitions.
claim_supported: Streaming dominates global recorded-music revenue, but country coverage and revenue quality vary.
limitation: Public summaries do not provide a Pakistan market estimate; premium market files may omit or aggregate Pakistan.

title: Global Music Report 2026
research_use: Epilogue context on streaming, performance rights, fraud, and Asian growth.
claim_supported: The global recorded-music market continued to grow through 2025, led by streaming.
limitation: Global growth cannot be assigned to Pakistan without country-level evidence.

title: Pakistan: PECA amendment raises censorship and due-process concerns
research_use: Platform governance, content removal, self-censorship, and regulatory risk.
claim_supported: Digital cultural circulation occurs within a changing and contested content-regulation environment.
limitation: A rights assessment should be paired with statutory text, court decisions, PTA notices, and creator testimony.

title: Pakistan 2023 Population and Housing Census
research_use: Population, urban-rural, provincial, age, education, and sampling context.
claim_supported: Audience and artist samples should be weighted or described against Pakistan’s demographic and geographic structure.
limitation: Census variables do not measure music consumption, platform access, or creative employment directly.

title: Pakistan Economic Survey, Information Technology and Telecommunications chapter
research_use: Macroeconomic, inflation, employment, digital economy, and telecom context.
claim_supported: Music-sector outcomes must be interpreted against inflation, exchange rates, unemployment, and the broader digital economy.
limitation: Creative and music industries are rarely isolated as a separate statistical sector.

title: YouTube Data API v3 documentation
research_use: Video metadata, channel metadata, comments where available, and reproducible capture procedures.
claim_supported: YouTube metrics can be collected programmatically with documented fields and quotas.
limitation: Historical view counts, deleted comments, recommendation exposure, geography, and private analytics are not generally available.
access_status: Public documentation; API credentials required for collection

title: Spotify Charts
time_scope: Daily and weekly depending on market and access
research_use: Peak rank, chart duration, and cross-market chart entry.
claim_supported: Chart placement provides a standardized attention indicator distinct from cumulative streams.
limitation: Historical coverage, market availability, anti-fraud adjustments, and download access can change; archive every extract.

title: Google Trends
research_use: Search attention around artists, tracks, events, and controversy.
claim_supported: Search interest can reveal attention beyond a single streaming platform.
limitation: Scores are sampled and normalized, not search counts; spelling, language, and topic selection materially affect results.

title: TikTok Creative Center
research_use: Short-form sound reuse, trend timing, and creator circulation where Pakistan data are available.
claim_supported: Short-form video can be measured as a distinct distribution and reuse channel.
limitation: Historical depth, country access, bot activity, and denominator transparency are limited.

title: Pakistan’s music-streaming platform Patari raises $200,000 in seed funding
research_use: Venture financing, exclusive releases, and local-platform growth strategy.
claim_supported: Local music-tech ventures attracted seed capital and attempted original-content financing.
limitation: Funding announcements do not establish profitability, retention, or long-term survival.
